pr.title: coverage: Replace the old span refiner with a single function
pr.description:
As more and more of the span refiner's functionality has been pulled out into separate early passes, it has finally reached the point where we can remove the rest of the old `SpansRefiner` code, and replace it with a single modestly-sized function.

~~There should be no change to the resulting coverage mappings, as demonstrated by the lack of changes to test output.~~

There is *almost* no change to the resulting coverage mappings. There are some minor changes to `loop` that on inspection appear to be neutral in terms of accuracy, with the old behaviour being a slightly-horrifying implementation detail of the old code, so I think they're acceptable.

Previous work in this direction includes:
- #125921
- #121019
- #119208
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage replaced the stateful pairwise `SpansRefiner` with a `pending`/`refined` span-refinement function. The reusable invariant is: sorted MIR-derived coverage spans that overlap but belong to different BCBs must not be combined or truncated into an artificial outer span; only same-BCB overlapping spans may remain pending, and list-adjacent same-BCB refined spans may be merged in a final dedup pass. This changes loop coverage mappings in a small way, including dropping the count attributed to the `loop` line in `loop-break`.
analysis.originalLogic: The old `SpansRefiner` walked sorted spans with `prev`/`curr`. Same-BCB spans were merged via `merge_from`; disjoint spans were emitted; overlapping spans with different BCBs invoked `cutoff_prev_at_overlapping_curr`, which used `cutoff_statements_at(curr.span.lo())` to retain only original merged statement spans with `span.hi() <= cutoff_pos`, then set the emitted span's high bound to the maximum high bound among those retained spans. The claimed effect was to "keep _only_ statements that end before `curr.lo()` (if any), and add the portion of the combined span for those statements."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation to test against is the old overlap handling: for an overlapping `prev`/`curr` pair with different BCBs, truncate `prev` at `curr.span.lo()` using its remembered `merged_spans`, emit it only if at least one remembered span ends at or before the cutoff, and set its high bound to the maximum high bound of retained spans. The corrected/new transformation instead retains an overlapping pending span only when `prev.bcb == curr.bcb`; otherwise it drops that pending span, then emits non-overlapping pending spans and finally calls `refined.dedup_by` to merge only list-adjacent mergeable spans. Do not treat the old cutoff as a general span-intersection operation: it depends on the history of spans merged into `prev`, not just the outer `prev.span`.
analysis.inputDomain: One bucket of `SpanFromMir` entries produced by `mir_to_initial_sorted_coverage_spans`, ordered by span low/high with relative dominance used for equal spans, after earlier coverage passes have already done hole-carving. Each entry has a source `Span` and a `BasicCoverageBlock`; the bucket can contain nested or partially overlapping spans, including a long outer span enclosing smaller spans with different control flow. Relevant examples are conditional `assert_ne!` expressions and a `loop` whose `break` changes the BCB inside the loop body.
analysis.trigger: Refining coverage mappings when one sorted coverage span overlaps a later span and the two spans have different BCBs, especially when a long outer span encloses an inner span with different control flow. The loop-break regression is triggered by a `loop` containing `if black_box(true) { break; }`.
preconditions: Input spans are already sorted within a bucket by span and relative BCB dominance.
Each `SpanFromMir` carries both a `Span` and its `BasicCoverageBlock`.
Earlier coverage passes have already extracted/refined much of the old span-refiner functionality.
The comparison must account for the old `PrevCovspan.merged_spans` history; testing only the visible outer spans does not model the old cutoff.
pitfalls: Assuming identical coverage mappings after the refactor: the PR explicitly says there is "almost" no change and permits minor `loop` mapping changes.
Using the old outer `prev.span` alone to reproduce `cutoff_statements_at`; the old code retained/truncated based on `merged_spans` and their maximum retained `hi`.
Treating the new rule as ordinary interval subtraction. It is BCB-sensitive: overlapping different-BCB spans are discarded rather than carved.
Merging overlapping spans solely because they are adjacent in the pending/refined vectors; the final merge requires `a.is_mergeable(b)`, i.e. equal BCBs.
Expecting the `loop` line to retain a hit count: the blessed test changes the counted loop line to an uncounted one.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/coverage/assert-ne.rs` to preserve the historically fragile overlapping-span case from `issue-84561.rs`, and `tests/coverage/loop-break.rs` (a modified copy of `tests/mir-opt/coverage/instrument_coverage.rs`) for the loop-break boundary. Compare `tests/coverage/*.cov-map` mappings and MIR `InstrumentCoverage` mappings, not just source-line hit counts. Program pairs should differ only in whether overlapping different-BCB spans reach the refiner (e.g. conditional assert expression or loop break) while keeping the same BCBs and span order, then assert the expected mapping/span boundaries. If blessing `loop-break`, also check the mir-opt version, as the test comment says: "If this test needs to be blessed, then the mir-opt version probably needs to be blessed too!"
evidence: coverage: Replace the old span refiner with a single function

There is *almost* no change to the resulting coverage mappings. There are some minor changes to `loop` that on inspection appear to be neutral in terms of accuracy, with the old behaviour being a slightly-horrifying implementation detail of the old code, so I think they're acceptable.
